evidence: The committed infrastructure definitions encrypt every store, volume, queue, stream and secret at rest, accept only TLS on every listener and endpoint, and keep their keys enabled and scoped, at the scanned commit
expected_output: the same checkov-results.json iac-baseline-clean reads (frameworks scanned, passed/failed counts, evaluated check ids, failed checks sorted), plus one observation row per failed check whose id the crosswalk checkov-3.3.11-to-2026.09.13.02 maps to KSI-SVC-SIN: check_id, check_name, framework, file, resource

assertions.description: Zero failed checks among the 69 checkov rule(s) the crosswalk maps to KSI-SVC-SIN — the committed infrastructure declares the state this indicator asks for, at the scanned commit.

caveats: Declared state only. Whether the key material is managed well, and whether data in transit inside a private network is protected, are beyond these rules. Corroborates the cloud plane; does not replace it.
notes: Derived from iac-baseline-clean by the crosswalk recipes/crosswalks/checkov-3.3.11-to-2026.09.13.02.json: the same collector, the same artifact, and 69 of its rules filed under KSI-SVC-SIN with a reviewed basis each. What a pass proves is DECLARED state — what the committed definitions say — and the register prints `declared` beside this method for that reason; it corroborates the cloud plane and never replaces it. Empty-set discipline — Guard: the collector emits this recipe's observation set only when at least one of its 69 mapped rules was evaluated in this run (present in checkov's passed or failed checks over every file of every detected framework); a tree where none of them applied gets no observation and the recipe stays unevidenced, so an empty set here is an exhaustively searched clean result over the whole of the mapped rules the run evaluated.

plain.checks: Reads the committed infrastructure for encryption in both directions: whether each store, volume, queue, stream and secret is defined with encryption at rest, whether each listener, distribution and endpoint refuses plaintext and old TLS, and whether the keys behind them are enabled and not open to every principal.
plain.violation: Some definition holds or moves information without encryption, or rests on a key whose control has been given away. It is what the code declares; encryption switched on later by hand, or data outside these resources, is not seen.
plain.fix: Enable encryption at rest on the resource, require TLS on the listener, raise the TLS policy, and tighten the key policy. Each failed check names the resource and the setting; where a customer-managed key is asked for and a platform key is deliberate, record the decision.
